problem: SOTA scene-graph/VLM object-goal navigation relies on large cloud-hosted frontier VLMs, so it cannot run locally on resource-constrained robots. Small local VLMs perform poorly zero-shot, and their verbose chain-of-thought output makes decoding too slow on embedded GPUs.
motivation: Cloud dependence adds latency and connectivity requirements, which blocks real deployment on mobile robots. Token generation dominates on-device latency (93.3% of runtime on a Jetson Orin AGX), so shortening outputs while keeping the reasoning matters most.
key_idea: Distill ~500 successful frontier-VLM reasoning traces into a 4B Qwen3.5 through SFT, then use closed-loop GRPO RL with a brevity reward (E-RLVR) plus quantization to cut output length and latency for on-device scene-graph OGN.
insight: A very small teacher-trace set (about 500) is enough to instill navigation ability, but student quality does not track teacher quality (Gemini teacher is better than GPT, yet the GPT student is better), and mixing teachers hurts (41% SR). RL alone gets only 36% SR, while SFT+RL keeps or improves SR (49) and cuts tokens from 535 to 149. Prompt-based brevity fails: 'Caveman' saves only 10.7% of tokens, and removing CoT saves 91.8% but raises queries from 9.41 to 15.61 and repetitions from 0.63 to 4.39 (the paper's 'increases 6.96x' contradicts these table values).
method: Scene-graph architecture: Hydra builds an online 3D scene graph (rooms, objects, frontiers) from RGB-D and odometry. Text lists rooms and objects with IDs, and visible object IDs are projected onto the image as set-of-marks.

High-level action space: the VLM picks navigate(obj_id), explore(room_id), find_new_rooms(), or done(). A PointGoal policy (DD-PPO in sim, SRU-based Fan et al. on the robot) executes the resulting pose goals.

SFT distillation: successful traces (481-532 samples per teacher) are logged from Gemini 3.1 Pro, GPT-5.4 and Claude Sonnet 4.6 on HM3D OVON train, using the privileged action space. Qwen3.5-4B is fine-tuned with LoRA, and the datasets are released.

E-RLVR: LoRA GRPO in a closed-loop Habitat loop, with N=4 completions per step forked into parallel simulator branches. The best branch continues. The reward combines done (weight 2.0), nav progress, exploration and brevity (weight 0.25), the last linear between a target length and a max length.
Quantization and deployment: llama.cpp on a Jetson Orin AGX, with IQ4_XS chosen from KLD and throughput profiling. It is tested on a handheld unit and a Unitree A2-W quadruped.

setting.backbone: Qwen3.5-4B (LoRA SFT + GRPO, IQ4_XS quantized for deployment); Claude Sonnet 4.6 / GPT-5.4 / Gemini 3.1 Pro (frozen) as teachers and cloud baselines
setting.training_data: ~481-532 successful frontier-model reasoning traces from HM3D OVON train for SFT; E-RLVR in Habitat on train episodes (750 steps)
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D with odometry, a 360° lookaround panorama, and a Hydra 3D scene graph (GT semantics in sim, Mask2Former on the real robot)
setting.action_space: high-level {navigate, explore, find_new_rooms, done}, executed by a PointGoal policy (Habitat forward 0.25 m / turn 30° in sim; continuous velocity on the robot)
setting.privileged: GT semantic annotations in simulation. Ablations use the privileged action space (shortest-path teleport) and a 1.0 m success radius. The main benchmark uses PointGoal execution and a 0.25 m success threshold.

results: On the full HM3D OVON val-unseen benchmark, the Claude Sonnet 4.6 pipeline reaches 39.7 SR / 19.7 SPL, competitive with OpenFrontier (39.0) and Uni-NaVid (39.5), and the distilled 4B student reaches 34.5 / 17.2. In the ablation, SFT lifts Qwen3.5-4B from 21% to 47% SR, SFT+RL reaches 49% with 72.1% fewer output tokens, and IQ4_XS quantization gives 47% SR. Episode latency on the Jetson drops from 305.2 s to 52.5 s (82.8% reduction).
limitations: Scene graphs cannot bind transient compositional semantics (e.g. a chair with a person on it), and sparse VLM queries may miss cues.
The ablations use a privileged action space, a 100-episode subset and a relaxed 1.0 m success radius, and the real-world evidence is qualitative only.
The student still trails the cloud models, and GT semantics are used in simulation.
